prompt.hi: Ab har poora, jaise 0 se 1, 6 barabar gaps mein bhi kata hai. Runner 0 se 7 gap daudta hai: kis fraction par ruka?
prompt.en: Now each whole, like 0 to 1, is also cut into 6 equal gaps. A runner runs 7 gaps from 0: which fraction?

reask.hi: Har poora 6 barabar gaps mein ho, toh 0 se 7 gap daudkar runner kis fraction par rukta hai?
reask.en: If each whole is in 6 equal gaps, what fraction does a runner stop on after 7 gaps from 0?

viewCaption.hi: Ab line ki dono taraf pattiyan hain: ek taraf ki pehli patti 8/8 tak poori rangi hai, aur doosri taraf ki har patti chhe barabar gaps mein. Doosri taraf ki patti ke gaps 0 se gino, aur dekho pehli patti kahan khatam hoti hai.
viewCaption.en: Now there are strips on both sides of the line: the first strip on one side is coloured in full, up to 8/8, and each strip on the other side is in six equal gaps. Count the other side's gaps from 0, and see where the first strip ends.

why.hi: har gap 1/6 hai, aur runner ne 7 gap daude, toh 7/6, yaani 1 aur 1/6
why.en: each gap is 1/6 and the runner ran 7 gaps, so 7/6, that is 1 and 1/6

whyShort.hi: 1/6 ke 7 gap, yaani 7/6
whyShort.en: 7 gaps of 1/6 make 7/6

whyAlt.hi: ginti 1 par na rukti hai, na wahan se nayi shuru hoti hai: upar wala number 0 se daude saare gap ginta hai
whyAlt.en: the count neither stops at 1 nor starts again from there: the top number counts all the gaps run from 0

answerViewCaption.hi: Doosri taraf 7/6 tak rang pehli patti poori bharta hai, aur agli patti ka ek gap. Pehli patti 1 hai, isliye 7/6, 1 ke thoda aage hai.
answerViewCaption.en: On the other side the colour up to 7/6 fills the first strip and one gap of the next. The first strip is 1, so 7/6 is just past 1.

simpler.hi: Runner wali taraf ek gap poore ka kitna hai, yeh socho, phir dekho usne aise kitne gap daude.
simpler.en: On the runner's side think how much of a whole one gap is, then see how many such gaps they ran.

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (a 0-to-2 line, fifths on top, tenths below), naming none of its numbers: same top number → same gap count; a bigger bottom number → shorter gaps → the same number of gaps stops sooner; then the child says which of 9/5 and 9/10 is past 1

say.hi: Socho, do fractions ka upar wala number ek jaisa hai, toh dono mein utne hi gap chalne hain. Jiska neeche wala number bada hai, uska har gap chhota hai, toh woh kam door jaata hai.
say.en: Picture two fractions with the same top number: both walk the same number of gaps. The one with the bigger bottom number has shorter gaps, so it goes less far.

simpler.hi: Dono mein gap ki ginti ek hai. Bas socho, jis taraf ek poore mein kam gaps hain, wahan ek gap lamba hota hai.
simpler.en: The gap count is the same. Just think: on the side with fewer gaps in one whole, each gap is longer.

sayAlt.hi: Do trainon mein 3-3 dibbe hain, ek ke dibbe lambe, ek ke chhote: ginti barabar, par lambe dibbon wali train zyada lambi hai. Line par bhi gaps ki ginti ek ho, toh jiske gap lambe, woh aage pahunchta hai.
sayAlt.en: Two trains have 3 coaches each, one with long coaches, one with short: the count is the same, but the long-coach train is longer. On the line too, when the gap count is the same, the one with longer gaps reaches further.

prompt.hi: Nayi line 0 se 2 tak hai: har poora 5 gaps mein bhi kata hai, 10 mein bhi. Kaun 1 ke aage hai: 9/5 ya 9/10?
prompt.en: A new line from 0 to 2: each whole is cut into 5 gaps, and into 10 too. Which is past 1: 9/5 or 9/10?

reask.hi: Kaun 1 ke aage hai: 9/5 ya 9/10?
reask.en: Which is past 1: 9/5 or 9/10?

viewCaption.hi: Ab line ki dono taraf pattiyan hain, dono 0 se shuru: ek taraf ki har patti paanch gaps mein, doosri taraf ki das chhote gaps mein. Pehli patti ka sira 1 hai, dono taraf ek hi jagah.
viewCaption.en: Now there are strips on both sides of the line, both starting at 0: each strip on one side is in five gaps, each on the other side in ten smaller gaps. The end of the first strip is 1, at the same place on both sides.

why.hi: dono mein 9 gap, par 1/5 wala gap do guna lamba: 9/5, yaani 1 aur 4/5, aur 9/10, 1 se pehle
why.en: both are 9 gaps, but a 1/5 gap is twice a 1/10: 9/5, that is 1 and 4/5; 9/10 is before 1

whyShort.hi: 1/5 wala gap do guna lamba, toh 9/5 aage
whyShort.en: a 1/5 gap is twice as long; 9/5 is further

whyAlt.hi: 9/10 mein 10 bada dekhkar usse aage samjha; par bada neeche wala number chhote gap banata hai, toh 9/10 ke 9 chhote gap aur 9/5 ke 9 lambe gap barabar door nahi jaate
whyAlt.en: you took 9/10 as further because 10 is bigger; but a bigger bottom number makes smaller gaps, so 9 small gaps of 9/10 and 9 long gaps of 9/5 do not go equally far

answerViewCaption.hi: Ek taraf 9/5 tak rang pehli patti ke paar jaata hai, doosri taraf 9/10 tak rang pehli patti ke andar ruk jaata hai. Isliye 9/5, 1 ke aage hai.
answerViewCaption.en: On one side the colour up to 9/5 goes past the first strip; on the other side the colour up to 9/10 stops inside the first strip. So 9/5 is past 1.

simpler.hi: Line par 1 dekho, aur gino ki dono taraf 1 tak kitne gap hain. Phir socho, dono fraction mein se kaun 1 ko paar karta hai.
simpler.en: Look at 1 on the line, and count how many gaps each side has up to 1. Then think which of the two fractions passes 1.

remediation.move: train between stations, on the then-card's own board (stations 0, 1, 2, each stretch in 5 equal parts): station 1 = 5/5; wherever the train halts is one real spot on the track with one number: the parts counted from 0, over 5; then a train from station 1 that goes 3 parts on

say.hi: Yeh stations 0 se 2 tak hain, aur har do stations ke beech 5 barabar gaps hain; station 1 par 5/5 hai. Train jahan rukti hai, uska number ek fraction hai: upar wala number 0 se gine gaps, aur neeche wala number 5.
say.en: These stations go from 0 to 2, with 5 equal gaps between each two stations; station 1 is at 5/5. Where the train stops, its number is one fraction: the top number is the gaps counted from 0, and the bottom number is 5.

simpler.hi: Station 1 ke aage bhi gap 0 se hi gine jaate hain, ginti 1 par rukti nahi. Isliye 1 ke baad wale mark ka upar wala number 5 se bada hota hai.
simpler.en: Past station 1 the gaps are still counted from 0; the count does not stop at 1. So a mark after 1 has a top number bigger than 5.

sayAlt.hi: Chhoti line socho, 0 se 1, sirf 2 barabar gaps: beech ka mark ek hi jagah hai, aur uska naam ek hi number hai, 1/2. Stations ki line par bhi train jahan ruke, uska naam ek fraction hai, do alag number nahi.
sayAlt.en: Picture a small line, 0 to 1, with just 2 equal gaps: the middle mark is one place, and its name is one number, 1/2. On the line of stations too, wherever the train stops, its name is one fraction, not two separate numbers.

viewCaption.hi: Stations ki line ab do poori pattiyan hain, ek ke baad ek, har patti paanch barabar gaps mein. Pehli patti rangi hai aur uske sire par 5/5 = 1 likha hai: wahi station 1 hai.
viewCaption.en: The line of stations is now two whole strips end to end, each in five equal gaps. The first strip is coloured and its end reads 5/5 = 1: that is station 1.

prompt.hi: Isi 0 se 2 ki line par ek doosri train station 1 se chali aur 3 gap aage ruki. Woh kis fraction par khadi hai?
prompt.en: On this line from 0 to 2, another train starts at station 1 and stops 3 gaps on. What fraction is it standing on?

reask.hi: Har do stations ke beech 5 barabar gaps hon, toh station 1 se 3 gap aage ruki train kis fraction par khadi hai?
reask.en: If there are 5 equal gaps between each two stations, at which fraction is a train that stopped 3 gaps past station 1?

viewCaption.hi: Line ab do poori pattiyan hain, har patti paanch barabar gaps mein. Sawaal wale mark tak ke gaps rangin hain: pehli patti poori, aur station 1 ke aage ke kuch gaps.
viewCaption.en: The line is now two whole strips, each in five equal gaps. The gaps up to the question mark are coloured: the first strip in full, and some gaps past station 1.

why.hi: station 1 = 5/5 hai, aur 3 gap aage 5 + 3 = 8, yaani 8/5, jo 1 aur 3/5 hai
why.en: station 1 is 5/5, and 3 gaps on makes 5 + 3 = 8 gaps: 8/5, which is 1 and 3/5

whyShort.hi: 1 = 5/5, aur 3 gap aage 8/5
whyShort.en: 1 is 5/5, and 3 gaps on is 8/5

whyAlt.hi: 3/5 toh station 0 aur station 1 ke beech aata hai, par yeh train station 1 paar kar chuki hai; uska fraction 1 se bada hona chahiye
whyAlt.en: 3/5 comes between station 0 and station 1, but this train has already passed station 1; its fraction must be bigger than 1

simpler.hi: Ginti 0 se karo, station 1 se nahi: station 1 tak ke gap bhi gino, aur uske aage ke bhi.
simpler.en: Count from 0, not from station 1: count the gaps up to station 1, and the ones after it too.

covered.hi: Aakhir mein dekha: upar wala number neeche wale se bada ho, toh fraction 1 ke aage aata hai.
covered.en: Last we saw: when the top number is bigger than the bottom one, the fraction comes after 1.

prompt.hi: Ek line 0 se 2 tak hai. 0 aur 1 ke beech 6 marks hain, aur 1 aur 2 ke beech bhi 6, sab barabar doori par. 0 se 9 gap chalo toh kis fraction par pahunchoge?
prompt.en: A line runs from 0 to 2. There are 6 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1, and 6 more between 1 and 2. Which fraction do you reach after moving 9 gaps from 0?

reask.hi: 0 se 2 ki line par har poore ke andar 6 marks barabar doori par lage hain; 0 se 9 gap chalkar kaunsa fraction aata hai?
reask.en: On a line from 0 to 2, each whole has 6 evenly spaced marks inside it; which fraction do you reach after 9 gaps from 0?

did.hi: 6 marks se gap nikala aur 0 se 9 gap gine
did.en: found each gap from 6 marks and counted 9 gaps from 0

why.hi: 6 marks se har poore ke 7 barabar gaps bante hain, toh har gap 1/7; 0 se 9 gap chalkar 9/7 aata hai, yaani 1 aur 2/7.
why.en: 6 marks make 7 equal gaps in each whole, so each gap is 1/7; 9 gaps from 0 reach 9/7, that is 1 and 2/7.

simpler.hi: Pehle dekho, 0 aur 1 ke beech ke 6 marks se kitne gaps bante hain; wahi ginti neeche wala number hai.
simpler.en: First see how many gaps the 6 marks between 0 and 1 make; that count is the bottom number.

viewCaption.hi: Dekho, 0 se 2 tak ki line ab do poori pattiyan hain, ek ke baad ek, dono saat barabar gaps mein. Ungli 0 par rakho aur gaps ek-ek karke gino.
viewCaption.en: Look, the line from 0 to 2 is now two whole strips end to end, both in seven equal gaps. Put a finger on 0 and count the gaps one by one.

covered.en: Today we saw that every fraction has a fixed place on the line, found by counting gaps. When the top number is bigger than the bottom number, the fraction comes after 1.
